entries.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy — SQL injection
entries.technique: parameterized queries and query structure validation
entries.passage: Curated note: prioritize parameterized queries, strict server-side validation, and safe error handling when scanner evidence indicates database-driven input reflection or query manipulation.

entries.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy — Cross-site scripting
entries.technique: context-aware output encoding with template hardening
entries.passage: Curated note: match the sink context before recommending fixes; combine output encoding, safer templating, and CSP as defense-in-depth rather than relying on CSP alone.

entries.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy — Access control vulnerabilities
entries.topic: authorization weaknesses across roles and workflows
entries.technique: server-side authorization checks on every sensitive action
entries.passage: Curated note: when evidence suggests direct object reference or missing role checks, emphasize centralized authorization and workflow-level access verification instead of client-side gating.

entries.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy — SSRF
entries.topic: outbound request handling and internal service exposure
entries.technique: allowlist outbound destinations and normalize URLs before fetch
entries.passage: Curated note: highlight URL canonicalization, destination allowlists, and outbound network segmentation when runtime evidence shows user-controlled fetch behavior or OAST callbacks.

entries.title: OWASP API Security Top 10 — Broken Object Level Authorization
entries.technique: enforce ownership and policy checks per object reference
entries.passage: Curated note: for API findings, map exposed object identifiers to ownership checks and require authorization decisions for every read or write path, including bulk and nested object endpoints.

entries.title: OWASP Top 10 — Security logging and monitoring failures
entries.technique: high-signal security telemetry with alert triage
entries.passage: Curated note: if the scan reveals drift, auth instability, or suspicious routing changes, recommend durable audit events and actionable monitoring so exploitation attempts are detectable and explainable.

entries.title: CWE-79 — Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
entries.technique: encode untrusted data for the output context
entries.passage: Curated note: use CWE mappings as a stable citation in reports, and align remediation language with the output context that failed rather than generic client-side sanitization.

entries.title: CWE-89 — Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
entries.technique: bind parameters and constrain query builders
entries.passage: Curated note: prefer remediation language that calls out prepared statements, query builder safety, and reduced database privileges when injection evidence is reproducible.

entries.title: HackTricks — XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
entries.technique: context-aware reflected, stored, and dom xss probing with sink analysis
entries.passage: Curated note: identify the exact reflection sink (HTML, attribute, JS, URL) before crafting a probe; HackTricks catalogs context-specific vectors and filter bypasses to confirm execution rather than mere reflection.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — XSS Injection
entries.technique: polyglot and filter-bypass payload sets for active xss fuzzing
entries.passage: Curated note: when seeding active XSS fuzzing, draw from the PayloadsAllTheThings XSS payload sets (polyglots, attribute breakouts, WAF bypasses) and match the candidate payloads to the detected output context.

entries.title: HackTricks — SQL Injection
entries.technique: error-based, union, and blind injection enumeration with sqlmap
entries.passage: Curated note: classify the injection (error/union/boolean/time-based) before exploitation; HackTricks maps each class to enumeration steps and DBMS-specific syntax that sqlmap can automate once a candidate parameter is confirmed.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — SQL Injection
entries.topic: sql injection payload selection for fuzzing
entries.technique: dbms-specific injection payload sets for active fuzzing
entries.passage: Curated note: seed injection fuzzing with DBMS-specific payload sets from PayloadsAllTheThings (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MSSQL, Oracle) and tailor the candidate strings to the database fingerprinted during recon.

entries.title: HackTricks — SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
entries.topic: outbound request abuse and internal exposure
entries.technique: cloud metadata, localhost, and url-parser bypass probing
entries.passage: Curated note: probe cloud metadata, loopback, and internal ranges, then test parser confusion and redirect chains; HackTricks details URL-scheme and host-encoding bypasses to defeat naive allowlists when SSRF is suspected.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — Server Side Request Forgery
entries.technique: host-encoding and scheme bypass payload sets for active ssrf fuzzing
entries.passage: Curated note: seed SSRF fuzzing with PayloadsAllTheThings bypass payloads (decimal/hex IPs, alternate schemes, DNS rebinding hosts) to test allowlist robustness on user-controlled fetch parameters.

entries.title: HackTricks — IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference)
entries.technique: object id enumeration and cross-account access verification
entries.passage: Curated note: enumerate sequential, encoded, and predictable identifiers across roles and accounts; HackTricks highlights confirming unauthorized read/write rather than relying on response codes alone when probing for IDOR.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — Insecure Direct Object References
entries.technique: identifier mutation and parameter-pollution test cases
entries.passage: Curated note: use PayloadsAllTheThings IDOR test cases (id wrapping, parameter pollution, array/JSON variants) to probe object references that recon flagged as user-controlled and authorization-sensitive.

entries.title: HackTricks — Server-Side Template Injection
entries.technique: engine fingerprinting via arithmetic probes then payload escalation
entries.passage: Curated note: fingerprint the template engine with arithmetic markers (e.g. {{7*7}}, ${7*7}) before escalating; HackTricks lists engine-specific escalation paths from evaluation to RCE once injection is confirmed.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — Server Side Template Injection
entries.technique: per-engine detection and escalation payload sets for active fuzzing
entries.passage: Curated note: seed SSTI fuzzing with PayloadsAllTheThings per-engine detection markers and escalation payloads, selecting the set that matches the template engine fingerprinted during probing.

entries.title: HackTricks — File Inclusion / Path Traversal
entries.technique: traversal sequence and encoding-bypass probing for lfi
entries.passage: Curated note: test plain, encoded, and nested traversal sequences plus PHP/wrapper tricks; HackTricks documents encoding and truncation bypasses to confirm file disclosure when a parameter influences a filesystem path.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — Directory Traversal
entries.topic: path traversal payload selection for fuzzing
entries.technique: encoded and nested traversal payload sets for active fuzzing
entries.passage: Curated note: seed traversal fuzzing with PayloadsAllTheThings sequences (double-encoded, nested ....//, and OS-specific paths) against parameters recon identified as file or path references.

entries.title: HackTricks — XXE (XML External Entity)
entries.topic: xml parser abuse and data exfiltration
entries.technique: inline and out-of-band entity injection probing
entries.passage: Curated note: test inline entity reads first, then out-of-band exfiltration when responses are blind; HackTricks covers parameter entities and protocol handlers to confirm XXE on XML-accepting endpoints.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — XXE Injection
entries.technique: inline, oob, and parameter-entity payload sets for active fuzzing
entries.passage: Curated note: seed XXE fuzzing with PayloadsAllTheThings entity payloads (inline read, OOB DTD, parameter entities) for endpoints that parse XML, SVG, or Office/document formats.

entries.title: HackTricks — Command Injection
entries.technique: separator and timing-oracle probing for command execution
entries.passage: Curated note: confirm command injection with timing oracles and out-of-band callbacks before destructive payloads; HackTricks lists shell separators and quoting bypasses for parameters that reach system commands.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — Command Injection
entries.topic: command injection payload selection for fuzzing
entries.technique: separator and bypass payload sets for active fuzzing
entries.passage: Curated note: seed command-injection fuzzing with PayloadsAllTheThings separator and filter-bypass payloads, preferring blind timing/OOB variants for parameters that may reach a shell.

entries.title: HackTricks — JWT (JSON Web Tokens)
entries.technique: alg confusion, none algorithm, and weak-secret probing
entries.passage: Curated note: inspect the JWT header for alg/kid abuse, test the none algorithm and RS256-to-HS256 confusion, and attempt weak-secret cracking; HackTricks details claim tampering once a forgery path is found.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — JSON Web Token
entries.technique: signature-bypass and key-injection test cases
entries.passage: Curated note: use PayloadsAllTheThings JWT test cases (alg none, key confusion, jwk/kid header injection) when a token is present, matching attacks to the signing algorithm observed.

entries.title: HackTricks — Open Redirect
entries.technique: redirect-parameter and url-parser bypass probing
entries.passage: Curated note: test absolute, protocol-relative, and obfuscated targets in redirect parameters; HackTricks documents parser-confusion bypasses that defeat naive same-host checks when validating open redirect.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — Open Redirect
entries.topic: open redirect payload selection for fuzzing
entries.technique: url-bypass payload sets for active fuzzing
entries.passage: Curated note: seed open-redirect fuzzing with PayloadsAllTheThings bypass payloads (//host, @host, encoded variants) for redirect, return, and next parameters discovered during crawling.

entries.title: HackTricks — CORS Bypass
entries.technique: origin reflection and null-origin trust probing
entries.passage: Curated note: test arbitrary, null, and subdomain origins while watching Access-Control-Allow-Origin/Credentials; HackTricks details when reflected origins with credentials enable cross-origin data theft.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — CORS Misconfiguration
entries.technique: origin-variation test cases for cors validation
entries.passage: Curated note: use PayloadsAllTheThings CORS origin-variation cases (trusted-suffix, prefix, null, regex bypass) to evaluate ACAO reflection on credentialed cross-origin endpoints.

entries.title: HackTricks — Login / Authentication Bypass
entries.technique: verb tampering, header override, and credential-logic probing
entries.passage: Curated note: combine HTTP verb tampering, override headers, and path normalization tricks to bypass auth or 403 gating; HackTricks catalogs header and routing bypasses to test before assuming access controls hold.

entries.title: HackTricks — Mass Assignment
entries.technique: hidden-field injection into create and update bodies
entries.passage: Curated note: inject privileged fields (role, isAdmin, owner) into create/update payloads and compare resulting state; HackTricks explains how framework auto-binding turns unguarded models into privilege escalation.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — Mass Assignment
entries.technique: privileged-field name sets for body fuzzing
entries.passage: Curated note: seed mass-assignment fuzzing with PayloadsAllTheThings privileged field names and nesting variants, injected into JSON and form bodies on create/update endpoints.

entries.title: HackTricks — HTTP Request Smuggling
entries.technique: cl.te and te.cl desync probing
entries.passage: Curated note: test CL.TE and TE.CL desync with timing-based detection before exploitation; HackTricks details header obfuscation that bypasses front-end normalization when smuggling is suspected.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — Request Smuggling
entries.technique: header-obfuscation desync test cases
entries.passage: Curated note: use PayloadsAllTheThings request-smuggling cases (header obfuscation, chunk-extension tricks) to probe desync on targets fronted by proxies or load balancers.

entries.title: HackTricks — Domain/Subdomain Takeover
entries.topic: dangling dns and unclaimed service detection
entries.technique: dangling cname enumeration and fingerprint matching
entries.passage: Curated note: enumerate subdomains, resolve CNAMEs, and match service fingerprints for unclaimed providers; HackTricks lists provider-specific takeover signatures to confirm a dangling reference is claimable.

entries.title: HackTricks — Web Vulnerabilities Methodology
entries.topic: sensitive path and source exposure discovery
entries.technique: backup, vcs, and config file discovery via content brute-forcing
entries.passage: Curated note: brute-force content for backup, VCS, and config artifacts (.git, .env, *.bak); HackTricks methodology prioritizes exposed source and secrets that convert low findings into high-impact disclosure.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — Upload Insecure Files (Zip Slip)
entries.topic: archive extraction path traversal payload selection
entries.technique: traversal archive entry names for active upload fuzzing
entries.passage: Curated note: when probing upload endpoints that accept archives, use PayloadsAllTheThings Zip Slip entry-name payloads (../ sequences inside ZIP/TAR entries) and compare against a benign control archive to detect missing entry-name sanitisation before extraction.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — XSLT Injection
entries.technique: document() based local file read and out-of-band payload sets for active fuzzing
entries.passage: Curated note: seed XSLT fuzzing with document()-based file-read and out-of-band payloads on endpoints that evaluate a user- or partially-user-controlled stylesheet, matching the payload to the fingerprinted XSLT processor (libxslt, Saxon, Xalan, .NET).

entries.title: HackTricks — SSRF URL format bypass (DNS rebinding class)
entries.topic: ssrf allowlist bypass via loopback-resolving hostnames
entries.technique: public hostnames resolving to loopback/internal IPs (nip.io, lvh.me class) to bypass hostname-string allowlists
entries.passage: Curated note: when a target's SSRF guard only checks the hostname string, test with public hostnames that resolve directly to loopback/link-local/metadata IPs — this confirms the guard does not validate the resolved IP and is a precondition for full DNS-rebinding TOCTOU attacks.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — DOM Clobbering
entries.technique: named id/name element injection to overwrite window/document globals
entries.passage: Curated note: when raw HTML injection is confirmed but script tags are filtered, use DOM Clobbering markup (same-id/name anchor or form elements) to overwrite application globals/config objects read without a typeof guard — a common gadget en route to script execution.

entries.title: PayloadsAllTheThings — Brute Force Rate Limit
entries.technique: bounded request-burst throttling checks across sensitive endpoints
entries.passage: Curated note: rate-limit checks should not stop at the login form — apply the same bounded-burst throttling test (expect 429/423/Retry-After/lockout) to password reset, registration, OTP verification, and coupon/invite redemption endpoints.

entries.title: HackTricks — Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
entries.topic: catastrophic backtracking regex denial of service
entries.technique: nested-quantifier trigger strings measured against differential timing baselines
entries.passage: Curated note: probe validation-style parameters (email, search, username) with classic catastrophic-backtracking trigger strings and compare latency against two control baselines; a large, reproducible timing spike indicates an exponential-backtracking validation regex.
